boundary_evidence: One contiguous run of the Nitro SDK's VRAM bank control (gx_vramcnt.c), 0x02053e1c..0x02054d38: 41 functions, gapless in config/arm9/delinks.txt, each one reads or writes the VRAM state block at data_020a6088 or the VRAMCNT registers 0x04000240..0x04000249, except the size helper GX_GetSizeOfX_ (0x02053e4c), which turns a bank mask into bytes for its two getters.

mwccarm emits .text in reverse source order, and the run reads as the SDK file top-down from the highest address: GX_VRAMCNT_SetLCDC_ (0x02054c80), the setters BG, OBJ, BGExtPltt, Tex, TexPltt, LCDC, SubBG, SubOBJ, SubBGExtPltt, SubOBJExtPltt, then resetBankForX_ (0x020541b8) and its wrappers, disableBankForX_ (0x0205402c) and its wrappers, the bank getters, and the size helper with its two callers at the bottom. Setters and wrappers the game never calls (OBJExtPltt, ClearImage, ARM7, ...) are absent, as a dead-stripped link leaves them.

The disable wrappers name all thirteen u16 fields of the state block in the SDK's order (BG, OBJ, BGExtPltt, OBJExtPltt, Tex, TexPltt, ClearImage, ARM7, LCDC, SubBG, SubOBJ, SubBGExtPltt, SubOBJExtPltt at offsets 2, 4, 0xe, 0x10, 8, 0xa, 0xc, 6, 0, 0x12, 0x14, 0x16, 0x18); the ext-palette ones also clear DISPCNT bit 30/31 of the matching engine. That fixes the layout of the block every member uses.

The three functions at the bottom (0x02053e1c, 0x02053e34, 0x02053e4c) are not in pret/pokediamond's GX_vramcnt.c, which holds only what Pokemon links. They are gx_vramcnt.c's size getters: the NitroSDK reconstruction in RushRE/SonicRushAdventure-Decomp (lib/NitroSDK/src/gx/gx_vramctrl.c) ends the file, after the bank getters, with static GX_GetSizeOfX_ (the same nine-bank size ladder as 0x02053e4c) and its GX_GetSizeOfBG .. GX_GetSizeOfARM7 wrappers. 0x02053e34 is GX_GetSizeOfTex and 0x02053e1c is GX_GetSizeOfTexPltt (GX::GetSizeOfTex and GX::GetSizeOfTexPltt here, still coined: pret's GX_vramcnt.c has no GX_GetSizeOf* to name them from); the other wrappers are not in this ROM. Reverse emission puts the end of the file at the bottom, so the TU's bottom edge is the file edge.
TOP EDGE: G2S_GetBG3CharPtr at 0x02054d38 is the first function of the promoted arm9/GX_BgCnt TU (src/engine/gx/GX_BgCnt.c, the SDK's BG-control getters).

BOTTOM EDGE: GX_InitGXState (0x02053d9c..0x02053e1c, src/GX_InitGXState.c) zeroes the thirteen state fields and the VRAMCNT A-I registers -- the SDK's GX_InitGXState, which lives with the state block in its own file (gx_state.c), not in gx_vramcnt.c. Below it, GX_Init (func_02053c40) calls it, then GX_HBlankIntr/GX_VBlankIntr, GX_DispOff, GX_DispOn, GX_SetGraphicsMode, GXS_SetGraphicsMode: gx.c, also reverse-ordered. Neither file is absorbed here.
No data, bss or RTTI: the state block is defined by the file below, and nothing but the 41 functions emits.
notes: Hand-assembled, not generated by `tubuild.py create`: tu_map cannot segment arm9/main, so there was no candidate id to create from. The schema follows arm9/GX_BgCnt.

The setters, the resetBankForX_ and disableBankForX_ wrappers and the bank getters carry their SDK names with C linkage (GX_SetBankFor*, GX_ResetBankFor*, GX_DisableBankFor*, GX_GetBankFor*: pret pokediamond arm9/lib/NitroSDK/src/GX_vramcnt.c, in its source order reversed), declared in include/nitro/gx/gx_vramcnt.h. GX_GetSizeOfTex and GX_GetSizeOfTexPltt are named from ntrtwl/NitroSDK libraries/gx/src/gx_vramcnt.c (pret's GX_vramcnt.c has no GX_GetSizeOf*); they were the coined GX::GetSizeOfTex and GX::GetSizeOfTexPltt. GX_SetBankForBGExtPltt and GX_SetBankForLCDC were address-named (func_02054748, func_02054430), and the three helpers were the coined Vram__Map, ResetVramBanks and DisableVramBanks; they now carry the SDK's names, the helpers being the SDK's statics GX_VRAMCNT_SetLCDC_, resetBankForX_ and disableBankForX_ kept at external C linkage.

The state block keeps its ROM name data_020a6088; its thirteen u16 fields are named after the SDK's VRAM users. The per-field data_020a608a..data_020a60a0 symbols are untouched; the wrappers reach them as fields of the block.
The file is written ROM-descending because mwccarm emits .text in reverse source order; the emitted object carries the 41 functions ascending 0x02053e1c..0x02054d38.
